text: At the Marrow Quay archives on Tuesday, curator Lenka Voss showed the Baywater Gazette a brittle 14th-century vellum booklet she identified as the Voskresen manuscript. “We checked the script, the loanwords, and the scribal shorthand ourselves,” she said, pointing to a page under lamp light. According to Voss, the text was written in Middle Low German, not Latin or any eastern Slavic tongue as earlier catalog notes suggested. The manuscript, acquired by the archive in 2019 from the estate of shipbroker Tomas Rehn, is believed to have been copied by a North Sea merchant scribe around 1380. Voss said two independent paleographers confirmed the language during a review last week.
